labels.audit: agree, with a recorded judgement call (minor 1)
labels.note: BTZ half: charted form (e0Manifold_isFutureDistinguishing) and SingularGXStructure form (e0SingManifold_isFutureDistinguishing), with [T2Space M] (DEC-66 (a)). BTZ~ half: isFutureDistinguishing_of_natGloballyHyperbolic takes as hypothesis d.natCausality.GloballyHyperbolic, which is GH in the natural topology (DEC-106). It concludes IsFutureDistinguishing d.causality, i.e. FD for the chart-generated ≪ (DEC-118 (a)). That is exactly the implication of l.2325 under the rulings, with no added hypothesis. The proof was read in full. It goes through the tarentin-free le_of_Iplus_eq_of_isCompact_image_diamond, applied with ι = toNat, which is continuous because T' ≤ natural, and uses natCausality_diamond. It is sound. natGloballyHyperbolic_iff is proved both ways, and it shows natural GH is exactly natural compactness of the chart-generated diamonds, so the hypothesis does not hide the conclusion. The general coarse-topology theorem behind it is non-vacuous with a BTZ line: in the model J⁺(Δ₀) the diamonds are compact in 𝐌³ (btzJ0_isCompact_val_image_diamond), which gives btzJ0_isFutureDistinguishing. A witness for the ruled hypothesis itself (natural GH with sing M ≠ ∅) is not built. That witness is DEC-118 (b) / WP-46d's deliverable. The auditor found no argument that it is unsatisfiable. Informally: at a BTZ point a natural neighbourhood contains the whole component (all θ), and the diamonds are D-bounded and τ-bounded. So the T_BTZ failure mode (x_ε escaping the BTZ neighbourhood) does not obviously recur. The gap is disclosed in the docstring, SCOPE (f) and REPORT. The previous auditor's question (WP-44c AUDIT-2) said that a ruling for reading (A) 'lets the three partial rows be marked', and DEC-118 (a) is that ruling.

Its dependence on the data (y₀, Φ, T') is disclosed in SCOPE (g), and D ↦ g·D invariance is proved (minor 3).

labels.label: lem:globally_hyperbolic_manifolds_maximal
labels.note: isFutureDistinguishing_of_base proves, from (e0ManifoldCausality M hM).GloballyHyperbolic (the paper's hypothesis, nothing added), IsFutureDistinguishing d.causality. That is the full statement of l.2359 under DEC-118 (a). The proof was read in full and is substantive: the projection is causal, D x = D y and p x = p y follow from I⁺(x) = I⁺(y), and the sheet is injective under a causally convex V. The statement does not assert 'M̃ GH'. That is only the paper's proof route (l.2361), and DEC-118 (b) assigns it to WP-46d. So the dispatch's 'leave the GH-of-M̃ part to WP-46d' takes no assertion away from this row. The T_BTZ counterexample (btzJ0Tilde_not_globallyHyperbolic) and the natural-causality counterexample stay as findings.
